title: Homework Now Names the Real Chapter, Not a Page Number | vitalii.no
description:
My kids' weekly homework used to say things like 's. 83, 84 og 85' — three bare page numbers from their Norwegian textbook, with no context. The app had no idea which chapter of the real book that was, so it could only echo the page numbers back instead of teaching toward the same grammar point or text type the class was actually covering that week.

New curriculum files now hold each child's real Cappelen Damm table of contents: chapter titles, start pages, and grammar focus, sourced from a parent's photo of the book or the publisher's own review copy. A book only counts as verified once at least two of its chapters match real page numbers pulled from past weekly plans. A shared textbooks module exports helpers to find the right book for a child and subject, pull the chapter out of a page range, and hand that chapter context into the nightly homework generator — without ever quoting the book's actual exercise text, and without retroactively re-firing homework sets that were already generated.

Every homework card on the family board now carries a bookLine() prefix naming the real chapter instead of a bare page number, and the nightly generation prompt mirrors that chapter's own grammar focus into the practice items it writes. Tonight's card reads 'Kapittel 4: Brøk' — not 's. 83'.
